records.title: [FEATURE] Add durable long-lived task execution layer for agentic workflows
records.relevance_note: LangChain4j issue detailing a durable execution module with checkpoints and journaling
records.reason_included: Provides design for durable tasks: checkpoints, journaling, resume after restart

claim_snippets.claim_text: Crash recovery — if the JVM restarts mid-workflow, the agent should resume from its last checkpoint rather than re-execute from scratch.
All lifecycle events (agent invocations, retries, pauses, cancellations, completions, failures) are recorded in an ordered, immutable journal per task.
ReplayingPlanner: on resume, replays completed invocations from the journal to fast-forward agent state.
CheckpointPolicy: NONE, AFTER_EACH_AGENT, AFTER_ROOT_CALL — controls when scope-aware checkpoints are taken at agentic scope boundaries.
Store-atomic compare-and-set: all status transitions use TaskExecutionStore.compareAndSetStatus() atomically to prevent a race between cancel and completion.

records.title: agentsh: Execution-Layer Security (ELS) for AI agents
records.relevance_note: agentsh tool supports workspace state checkpointing and recovery
records.reason_included: Describes commands for creating and restoring workspace checkpoints, including auto-checkpoint before risky commands.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Create snapshots of workspace state for recovery: use 'agentsh checkpoint create', 'checkpoint rollback' to restore the workspace state.
Auto-checkpoint: when enabled, agentsh automatically creates checkpoints before risky file operations (e.g., rm, mv, git reset).

records.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Workflows - Checkpoints
records.relevance_note: Official docs for agent workflow checkpointing
records.reason_included: Shows how workflow checkpoints capture full state and how to resume workflows from checkpoints.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Checkpoints capture the entire state of the workflow, including the current state of all executors, all pending messages, requests/responses, and shared states at each superstep.
To enable checkpointing, provide a CheckpointManager or CheckpointStorage when running the workflow; checkpoints can be accessed via run.Checkpoints or SuperStepCompletedEvent.
Workflows can resume from a specific checkpoint on the same run instance or by rehydrating a new run from the checkpoint state.
Executors must override OnCheckpointingAsync to save their state into the workflow context so it is captured in the checkpoint.

records.title: Build durable AI agents with LangGraph and Amazon DynamoDB
records.relevance_note: LangGraph and DynamoDB checkpointing design (AWS blog)
records.reason_included: Explains LangGraph's checkpoint/thread model and DynamoDBSaver persistence for agent state resumption.

claim_snippets.claim_text: In LangGraph, a checkpoint is a snapshot of the graph state at each super-step, containing configuration, metadata, state channel values, next nodes, and task info; these are persisted to allow restoring thread state later.

Persistence enables advanced features like human-in-loop review, replay, and resumption: by default LangGraph's InMemorySaver stores state only in memory (ephemeral), so production needs a durable store to resume after crashes.

The DynamoDBSaver stores small checkpoints (<350KB) directly in DynamoDB (with metadata) and large checkpoints (≥350KB) in S3 (with a pointer in DynamoDB); on resume it retrieves them to reconstruct state.
LangGraph uses a 'thread_id' to identify a sequence of runs for persistence; a thread must be created before execution for checkpoints to persist state.

claim_locations.locator: Sections 'Persistence is what enables advanced features' and 'Why persistence matters'

records.title: Autonomous Agent Migration Framework (AAMF)
records.relevance_note: AAMF migration framework's checkpoint and resume design
records.reason_included: Shows that all execution state is saved to files and how resume works after interruption.

claim_snippets.claim_text: All execution state is persisted to `.aamf/migration/.../state/checkpoint.json` after every phase or task completion; the checkpoint records phase cursors, completed/failed tasks, outputs, token usage, etc.

To resume an interrupted migration, use `--resume`; the orchestrator skips completed phases and resumes from saved cursors. A backup checkpoint (state/checkpoint.backup.json) is kept for corruption recovery.
Failed agent tasks are retried up to a max (default 3); infrastructure errors (file-lock, OOM, network) are retried separately.

claim_locations.locator: README.md under 'To resume an interrupted migration'

records.title: Agent Continuations for Resumable AI Workflows
records.exception_reason: Outside the primary window but retained for explicit continuation snapshot and resume mechanics in agent workflows.
records.relevance_note: SnapLogic blog on agent continuations (snapshot/resume state)
records.reason_included: Captures agent state in continuations (event log, pending actions) enabling pause and resume with no loss.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Agent Continuations snapshot the full state of an agent (including pending tool calls and nested sub-agents) at any step and can later resume the agent exactly where it left off.
Every agent interaction (LLM call, tool execution) is recorded in a structured 'messages' event log; a continuation holds this array plus metadata about pending actions and approval flags.
After human approval, the updated continuation is returned and the agent reconstructs its entire workflow from it, resuming execution with no lost progress.

records.title: Building AI agents that overcome the complexity cliff
records.exception_reason: Pre-2025 source on durable execution and event logging
records.relevance_note: Temporal.io blog on durable execution via event logs and replay
records.reason_included: Advocates logging every step and replaying execution history to resume computation without restart.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Durable Execution requires automatic state persistence: every step is immutably logged by default so progress survives process death without additional code.
Replay capability: execution can resume from any point by reconstructing state from the event log, avoiding re-running completed steps.
Without durable execution, an agent would restart from the beginning on failure; with event-log replay, the agent can rebuild state up to the failure point and resume at the next step.

records.title: VS Code extension crash can leave a thread permanently stuck in "thinking" with queued input · Issue #14127
records.relevance_note: Concrete persisted-state corruption report after mid-turn crash.
records.reason_included: Direct evidence for missing terminal markers and unusable resumed threads.

claim_snippets.claim_text: After an extension crash during an active turn, the reopened thread can remain permanently in a thinking state, cannot be stopped, and queues new input instead of starting a new turn.
The reporter inspected the persisted rollout or session file and found it ended with a response_item whose payload type was reasoning, with no completed or aborted terminal event afterward.
The expected recovery state proposed in the issue is to mark the interrupted turn as aborted, interrupted, or recoverable draft rather than leaving it permanently active.

records.title: Add ability to update or migrate thread references when projects are moved to new locations · Issue #11022
records.relevance_note: Shows workspace-path drift breaking stored thread references.
records.reason_included: High-value failure mode for project-bound thread state.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When a project folder is moved, existing conversation threads can become inaccessible because thread references are hardcoded to the original file path.
The issue states that threads are stored in an internal database with absolute file path references, making relocation break access.
The requested recovery mechanism is a path-migration flow that updates thread references to the new project location.

records.title: Changelog - Claude Code Docs
records.relevance_note: Official release-note evidence for multiple state and resume fixes.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete, state-specific fixes across resume, worktrees, hooks, and compaction.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A March 14 fix addressed a race where stale-worktree cleanup could delete an agent worktree that had just been resumed after a previous crash.
A March 14 change made --resume faster on fork-heavy and very large sessions, reducing peak memory by roughly 100-150MB.
A March 14 change made SendMessage auto-resume stopped agents in the background instead of returning an error.
A March 11 fix made sessions resumed from a worktree switch back to that worktree, and fixed SessionStart hooks firing twice on --resume or --continue.
A March 11 change improved post-interrupt recovery so the Up arrow restores the interrupted prompt and rewinds the conversation in one step.

records.title: sessions-index.json not updated, causing claude --resume to show stale or missing sessions · Issue #25032
records.relevance_note: Separates durable session data from stale resume index state.
records.reason_included: Direct evidence for authoritative-log versus derived-index mismatch.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue reports that claude --resume shows only a random subset of old sessions even though recent session .jsonl files are present on disk.
The reported root cause is that sessions-index.json files under ~/.claude/projects/ are missing or stale and are not updated when new sessions are created.
The issue explicitly distinguishes intact underlying session data from broken resume discoverability, implying the resume picker depends on derived index files rather than raw session logs.

records.title: Remote Control causes repeated .claude.json corruption on Windows (MSYS/Git Bash) · Issue #28965
records.relevance_note: Concrete corruption report on the main local session-state file.
records.reason_included: High-value evidence for concurrent-write repair requirements.

claim_snippets.claim_text: With Remote Control enabled on Windows MSYS or Git Bash, the .claude.json session state file repeatedly corrupts and forces re-login.
The issue reports 11 corrupted backup files created in about 30 minutes, with several timestamps only milliseconds apart, which the author interprets as evidence of a race between concurrent writers.
The workaround reported is to disable remote connections, and the proposed fix is atomic temp-file plus rename writes and file locking for the session-state file.
